document: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that enables computers to understand human language.
Machine learning is a field of artificial intelligence where systems learn patterns from data without explicit programming.
Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses artificial neural networks with many layers.
Python is a high level programming language widely used for web development, data science, and artificial intelligence.
Java is an object oriented programming language designed for portability across different platforms.
An operating system manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides services for applications.
A database is an organized collection of structured information that allows efficient storage and retrieval.
SQL is a language used to manage and query relational databases.
Cloud computing provides computing resources such as servers and storage over the internet.
The Internet of Things connects physical devices through the internet so they can exchange data.
Artificial intelligence is the simulation of human intelligence by machines capable of reasoning and learning.
Computer vision enables computers to interpret and understand information from images and videos.
Reinforcement learning trains an agent to make decisions by maximizing cumulative rewards.
Supervised learning trains a model using labeled examples to predict future outcomes.
Unsupervised learning discovers hidden patterns from unlabeled data.
A neural network is a computational model inspired by biological neurons and is widely used in deep learning.
Overfitting occurs when a machine learning model memorizes training data and performs poorly on unseen data.
Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data.
Data science combines statistics, programming, and domain knowledge to extract insights from data.
Big data refers to extremely large datasets that require specialized tools for storage and analysis.
Blockchain is a decentralized digital ledger that securely records transactions.
Cybersecurity protects computer systems, networks, and data from digital attacks.
Encryption converts readable information into encoded text to protect confidentiality.
Hashing transforms input data into a fixed length value commonly used for data integrity.
A compiler translates source code into machine code before execution.
An interpreter executes source code line by line without producing a separate executable.
An API allows different software applications to communicate with each other.
Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of a problem.
A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out principle.
A queue is a linear data structure that follows the First In First Out principle.
The kernel is the central component of an operating system responsible for managing hardware resources and system processes.
A process is a program that is currently being executed along with its allocated memory and resources.
A thread is the smallest unit of execution within a process and shares resources with other threads in the same process.
Virtualization allows multiple virtual machines to run on a single physical computer using shared hardware resources.
Docker is a container platform that packages applications together with their dependencies for consistent deployment.
Kubernetes is a container orchestration system that automates deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.
Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in source code during software development.
GitHub is a cloud platform for hosting Git repositories and enabling collaborative software development.
Linux is an open-source operating system known for stability, flexibility, and strong community support.
Microsoft Windows is a family of operating systems that provides a graphical user interface for personal computers.
Cache memory stores frequently accessed data close to the processor to reduce memory access time.
Random Access Memory temporarily stores data and instructions that are actively used by the processor.
Read Only Memory permanently stores firmware required to initialize computer hardware.
The Central Processing Unit executes instructions and performs arithmetic and logical operations.
A Graphics Processing Unit accelerates image rendering and massively parallel numerical computations.
Load balancing distributes incoming requests across multiple servers to improve performance and availability.
Latency is the time delay between sending a request and receiving a response.
Bandwidth represents the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a network in a given time.
The Domain Name System translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
An IP address uniquely identifies a device connected to a computer network.
HTTP is a protocol used to transfer web pages and other resources between clients and servers.
HTTPS secures HTTP communication using encryption provided by Transport Layer Security.
TCP is a reliable transport protocol that guarantees ordered and error-checked delivery of data.
UDP is a lightweight transport protocol that prioritizes speed over guaranteed delivery.
A firewall monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic according to security rules.
Phishing is a cyberattack that tricks users into revealing sensitive information through deceptive messages.
Malware is malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems.
Ransomware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to restore access.
A digital signature verifies the authenticity and integrity of electronic documents.
Authentication verifies the identity of a user before granting access to a system.
Authorization determines what actions an authenticated user is permitted to perform.
Database normalization organizes tables to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.
A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a database table.
A foreign key establishes a relationship between records in different database tables.
Database indexing improves query performance by allowing faster data retrieval.
A binary tree is a hierarchical data structure in which each node has at most two children.
A graph consists of vertices connected by edges and is commonly used to represent relationships.
A linked list stores elements as nodes connected through references rather than contiguous memory.
Binary search efficiently locates an element in a sorted collection by repeatedly dividing the search interval.
Quicksort is a divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that partitions elements around a pivot.
Merge sort recursively divides a collection into smaller parts before merging them in sorted order.
Dynamic programming solves complex optimization problems by storing solutions to overlapping subproblems.
A greedy algorithm builds a solution by repeatedly making locally optimal decisions.
A decision tree predicts outcomes by recursively splitting data according to feature values.
Logistic regression is a classification algorithm that estimates the probability of discrete outcomes.
K-means clustering partitions data into groups by minimizing distances between points and cluster centers.
Dimensionality reduction decreases the number of input features while preserving important information.
Feature engineering transforms raw data into meaningful variables that improve machine learning models.
Gradient descent iteratively adjusts model parameters to minimize a loss function.
An activation function introduces nonlinearity into a neural network, enabling it to learn complex patterns.
A microprocessor is an integrated circuit that performs the functions of a central processing unit on a single chip.
A motherboard is the main circuit board that connects and allows communication between computer components.
A hard disk is a non-volatile storage device used to permanently store digital information.
A solid state drive stores data using flash memory, providing faster access speeds than traditional hard drives.
Firmware is low-level software permanently stored in hardware to control the operation of electronic devices.
Booting is the process of starting a computer and loading the operating system into memory.
A scheduler determines the order in which processes or threads receive CPU time for execution.
Deadlock is a situation where multiple processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.
Paging is a memory management technique that divides memory into fixed-size blocks for efficient allocation.
Segmentation is a memory management method that organizes memory into variable-sized logical sections.
Socket programming enables applications to communicate over a network using endpoints called sockets.
Ethernet is a widely used networking technology for connecting devices within a local area network.
Wi-Fi is a wireless networking technology that allows devices to access networks without physical cables.
A router forwards data packets between different computer networks based on destination addresses.
A network switch connects devices within the same network and forwards data using MAC addresses.
A modem converts digital signals into forms suitable for transmission over communication channels.
Packet switching divides data into smaller packets that are transmitted independently across a network.
A MAC address is a unique hardware identifier assigned to a network interface for local communication.
A subnet is a logical division of a larger network that improves organization and traffic management.
A virtual private network creates an encrypted connection that securely transmits data over public networks.
A session stores user-specific information across multiple interactions with a web application.
A cookie is a small piece of data stored in a user's browser to remember preferences or session details.
HTML is the standard markup language used to structure content on web pages.
CSS is a stylesheet language used to control the appearance and layout of web pages.
JavaScript is a programming language that adds interactive behavior to websites.
Frontend development focuses on creating the user interface and interactive components of web applications.
Backend development involves building server-side logic, databases, and APIs that power applications.
Full stack development combines frontend and backend technologies to build complete web applications.
Responsive design ensures that web pages automatically adapt to different screen sizes and devices.
A REST API follows architectural principles that enable communication between client and server using HTTP methods.
JSON is a lightweight data interchange format commonly used for exchanging structured information between systems.
XML is a markup language designed to store and transport structured data in a human-readable format.
Debugging is the process of identifying, analyzing, and fixing errors in software.
Software testing evaluates a program to verify that it behaves correctly and satisfies specified requirements.
Unit testing verifies the correctness of individual functions or components in isolation.
Integration testing checks whether multiple software components work correctly when combined.
Agile methodology is a software development approach that emphasizes iterative delivery and customer collaboration.
Scrum is an Agile framework that organizes software development into short iterative cycles called sprints.
DevOps is a set of practices that integrates software development and IT operations to enable faster delivery.
Continuous integration automatically merges and tests code changes to detect issues early.
Continuous deployment automatically releases validated software changes to production environments.
Transfer learning improves performance by adapting knowledge learned from one task to another related task.
Cross validation estimates a machine learning model's performance by repeatedly training and testing on different data splits.
Precision measures the proportion of predicted positive instances that are actually positive.
Recall measures the proportion of actual positive instances that are correctly identified by a model.
The F1 score combines precision and recall into a single metric using their harmonic mean.
A confusion matrix summarizes classification performance by comparing predicted labels with actual labels.
A recommendation system suggests relevant items to users based on preferences, behavior, or similarities.
Generative AI creates new content such as text, images, audio, or code by learning patterns from existing data.
A large language model is a neural network trained on vast amounts of text to understand and generate human-like language.
A Bloom filter is a probabilistic data structure that efficiently checks whether an element may exist in a set.
A trie is a tree-based data structure used for efficient storage and retrieval of strings.
A heap is a specialized tree structure that maintains the highest or lowest priority element at the root.
A priority queue stores elements according to priority rather than insertion order.
Breadth First Search explores graph vertices level by level using a queue.
Depth First Search explores graph paths by visiting one branch completely before backtracking.
Dijkstra's algorithm computes the shortest path from a source node to all reachable nodes in a weighted graph.
A hash table stores key-value pairs and provides fast lookup through a hash function.
Object-oriented programming organizes software using objects that combine data and behavior.
A class is a blueprint that defines the properties and behaviors of objects.
An object is a runtime instance of a class containing its own data and methods.
Encapsulation restricts direct access to an object's internal data while exposing controlled interfaces.
Inheritance allows one class to acquire the properties and methods of another class.
Polymorphism enables the same interface to represent different underlying implementations.
Abstraction hides implementation details while exposing only essential functionality.
Exception handling provides mechanisms for detecting and recovering from runtime errors.
Multithreading enables multiple threads to execute concurrently within a single process.
Synchronization coordinates concurrent access to shared resources to prevent inconsistencies.
A race condition occurs when multiple threads access shared data in an unpredictable order.
A mutex is a synchronization mechanism that ensures only one thread accesses a critical section at a time.
A semaphore controls access to shared resources by maintaining a count of available permits.
A star schema organizes a data warehouse using one fact table connected to multiple dimension tables.
A data warehouse stores integrated historical data optimized for reporting and analytics.
A data lake stores structured and unstructured data in its original format for future analysis.
A NoSQL database stores data using flexible models such as documents, key-value pairs, or graphs.
A document database stores information as self-contained documents rather than rows and columns.
A key-value store manages data as unique keys associated with corresponding values.
A graph database represents data as nodes and relationships for efficient traversal of connected information.
Sharding distributes database records across multiple servers to improve scalability.
Replication maintains multiple copies of data across systems to improve availability and fault tolerance.
Load testing evaluates system performance under expected levels of user activity.
Stress testing measures how a system behaves under workloads beyond its intended capacity.
Regression testing verifies that recent code changes have not introduced defects into existing functionality.
Code review is the systematic examination of source code to improve quality and detect defects.
Software architecture defines the high-level structure and organization of a software system.
Microservices architecture builds applications as independent services that communicate through lightweight protocols.
A monolithic architecture develops all application components as a single deployable unit.
Serverless computing allows developers to run applications without managing the underlying infrastructure.
Edge computing processes data closer to where it is generated to reduce latency.
A distributed system consists of multiple computers that work together as a single coordinated system.
Fault tolerance enables a system to continue operating despite failures of individual components.
Scalability is the ability of a system to handle increasing workloads by expanding available resources.
Availability measures how consistently a system remains operational and accessible to users.
Latency optimization reduces delays in processing and communication to improve response times.
Anomaly detection identifies unusual patterns in data that differ significantly from expected behavior.
Model inference is the process of using a trained machine learning model to generate predictions.
Prompt engineering involves designing effective inputs that guide large language models toward desired outputs.
A vector database stores high-dimensional embeddings to enable efficient similarity search.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines information retrieval with language generation to produce more accurate responses.
An embedding is a numerical vector representation that captures the semantic meaning of data such as text or images.
